job.style: a conversation between a teacher and two students

passage: Teacher: Today, let us discuss the properties of whole numbers. Rohan, if we subtract 3 from 7, what do we get? Rohan: That is 4, teacher. Teacher: Correct. Now, what if we subtract 7 from 3? Rohan: That would also be 4, because subtraction is just finding the difference. Teacher: Actually, that is a common mistake. Subtraction is not commutative; 7 minus 3 is 4, but 3 minus 7 is not a whole number. Priya: I see. Does that mean 0 acts like a special number for subtraction, just like it does for addition? Teacher: Not quite, Priya. Adding 0 to any number keeps it the same, so 0 is the identity element for addition. However, if you subtract 0 from a number, the result is the number itself, but subtracting a number from 0 does not give you that number back. Therefore, 0 is not the identity element for subtraction. Remember, natural numbers start from 1, while whole numbers include 0 and all natural numbers. When we place these on a number line, whole numbers extend infinitely to the right, starting from 0. Always check the order of your numbers carefully before performing operations.

items.evidence: Subtraction is not commutative; 7 minus 3 is 4, but 3 minus 7 is not a whole number.
items.q: Meena works out 5 minus 9 and says it is the same as 9 minus 5. What is wrong?
options: Swapping the numbers changes the answer
Both give 4, so she is right
Only 9 minus 5 can be worked out
The answer is 4 only for small numbers
items.explain: Subtraction is not commutative: 7 minus 3 is 4, but 3 minus 7 is not a whole number.

wrong.why: thinks a - b equals b - a
thinks subtraction of whole numbers always works
thinks the rule depends on the size of numbers

items.evidence: However, if you subtract 0 from a number, the result is the number itself, but subtracting a number from 0 does not give you that number back.
items.q: Why does 0 fail to be the identity element for subtraction?
options: Taking a number from 0 does not return that number
Taking 0 from a number does not return that number
Adding 0 to a number does not return that number
Taking 0 from 0 does not return zero
items.explain: An identity must work in both orders; 0 minus a number does not give that number back.

wrong.why: reverses which order of subtraction fails
picks a case that nobody could test wrongly

items.evidence: Remember, natural numbers start from 1, while whole numbers include 0 and all natural numbers.
items.q: How are whole numbers different from natural numbers?
options: Whole numbers also include the number 0
Whole numbers stop at some large number
Whole numbers leave out the number 1
Whole numbers are the same set as natural numbers
items.explain: Natural numbers start from 1, while whole numbers include 0 and all the natural numbers.

wrong.why: thinks the numbers stop at some big number
thinks counting starts from 0 so 1 is dropped
thinks the two sets are identical

items.evidence: When we place these on a number line, whole numbers extend infinitely to the right, starting from 0.
items.q: Sam reaches the end of his drawn number line. What should he understand about whole numbers?
options: They keep going on past the drawn end
They stop where the drawn line stops
They begin again from zero at the end
They go on only to the left of 0
items.explain: Whole numbers extend infinitely to the right from 0, so a drawn line shows only part of them.

wrong.why: thinks the line's arrow shows an end
thinks the numbers repeat in a cycle
mixes up the direction of the number line
